column1: # Desktop / GUI. KDE Plasma on CachyOS. Installed on BOTH machines.
# NB: "desktop" here means the graphical SESSION, not the desktop machine.
# The machine-role manifests are gaming.tsv and creative.tsv, and the
# hardware ones are cpu-*.tsv and gpu-*.tsv. This file predates all of them
# and the name is now ambiguous; do not "fix" it by moving desktop-machine
# NB: this list does NOT include Plasma itself. The CachyOS KDE edition installs
# the workspace, SDDM/plasmalogin, Breeze, the portal and the core KDE apps at
# install time. Listing them here would be redundant, and `--needed` would make
# them no-ops anyway. What IS listed: the things the edition does not give you,
# plus the KDE apps actually used day to day, so a rebuild is reproducible.
# NB: the reason this file is short again is worth recording. It briefly carried
# a ~45-package niri + Noctalia session - compositor, shell, portals, polkit
# agent, notification daemon, screen locker, idle daemon, clipboard manager,
# GTK/Qt theming, and replacements for six KDE apps. All of that is what Plasma
# provides out of the box, and measured on this machine the whole Plasma session

PACKAGE name and FAMILY name differ - the fonts inside are Nerd Fonts' patch of Cascadia Code, which renames the family to "CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font" (files: CaskaydiaCoveNerdFont-*.ttf). "Cascadia Code NF" matches NOTHING and fc-match silently substitutes Adwaita Sans; that was live for weeks. scripts/doctor.sh now checks it. Replaced Maple Mono, whose AUR package failed to install in the VM

ships BOTH "Adwaita Sans" (the system UI font here) and "Adwaita Mono"; only Sans is used - monospace is CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font. Family strings are what ~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf matches on, so they are load-bearing - and Adwaita Sans is specifically what a WRONG monospace family falls back to, so a broken mono font looks like "everything is Adwaita" rather than like an error

GitHub's own UI font. NOT decoration: github.com's CSS asks for "Mona Sans" first and, with the family absent locally, falls through its own stack to Noto Sans - which is exactly what the site was rendering in. Installing it makes the first entry resolve whether or not the webfont loads (a content blocker's "block remote fonts" is the usual reason it does not)

GitHub's code font, the monospace half of the same problem: without it, github.com code blocks fell through to Liberation Mono. NB: the family to check is "Monaspace Neon", not the package name - see the CaskaydiaCove row above for what that mistake costs

column5: Anthropic's OFFICIAL Linux build (Chat + Cowork + Claude Code), in beta since 2026-06-30. Official support is Debian/Ubuntu ONLY, via Anthropic's apt repo - the docs tell Arch and Fedora users to run the CLI instead. So this AUR package is the path: it downloads the official .deb from downloads.claude.ai and repackages its payload, plus symlink shims for the Debian paths Cowork hardcodes (virtiofsd, OVMF). Not a third-party rebuild. The qemu-system-x86 + edk2-ovmf + virtiofsd deps are Cowork's VM sandbox and are parity with the .deb's Recommends, which apt installs by default - NOT AUR bloat. See SETUP-GUIDE Phase 5 for the KVM prerequisites, and Phase 4 for the memory tension with the Docker Desktop argument

column1: # NOTHING is packaged here any more, and the empty section is the point: the
# Catppuccin Latte Blue colour scheme, the splash and the WhiteSur cursors all
# Plasma. Window decoration stays KDE's own Breeze, recoloured by the scheme.
# NB: whitesur-icon-theme used to be the one row here. The icon theme is now
# Breeze, which Plasma already ships - so there is no icon package to install,
# and one fewer AUR build that can fail on a first bootstrap. WhiteSur moved to
# packages/unwanted.tsv, because dropping a row from THIS file would only stop
# it being reinstalled and would never take the 195 MB off a disk that has it.
# The WhiteSur cursors are unaffected: they are an external, not that package.
# NB: the launcher button's Catppuccin icon is not packaged either - it is a PNG
# pointed at by the kde-theme script through plasmashell's scripting API.
# NB: there is NO CATPPUCCIN LOCK SCREEN PACKAGE to add here, checked
# 2026-09-04. catppuccin/kde's look-and-feel packages contain only a `defaults`
# file - no lockscreen QML anywhere in the repo - and catppuccin's ports list
# has an SDDM theme but no kscreenlocker one. This machine does not run SDDM
# either; the display manager is plasmalogin. The lock screen is themed instead
# by the colour scheme (which its greeter already follows) plus a wallpaper key,
# both written by the kde-theme script. See the long note there.
# NB: intel-media-driver moved to packages/gpu-intel.tsv - it is a GPU fact,
# and setting LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD on an AMD card kills VA-API outright.
# libva-utils stays here because `vainfo` is vendor-neutral and doctor.sh

column5: provides `vainfo`, which is how doctor.sh proves VA-API actually initialised rather than that a driver package is installed

provides `vulkaninfo`. Vendor-neutral and needed on BOTH machines: a missing Vulkan driver does not error, the loader silently falls back to llvmpipe, and vulkaninfo is the only way to see which one you got
